title: Class Properties and Methods
ques: Create a TypeScript class named **`BankAccount`** with fields for `accountNumber` (string) and `balance` (number). Implement methods for `deposit(amount: number)` and `getBalance(): number`.
explanation: TypeScript classes provide full object-oriented syntax with strict property type annotations and constructor parameter validation.

title: Access Modifiers: Public, Private, and Protected
ques: Contrast the **`public`**, **`private`**, and **`protected`** access modifiers in TypeScript. Write a class hierarchy demonstrating the visibility of each modifier in child classes and outside code.
explanation: Access modifiers enforce encapsulation. `public` is accessible universally, `protected` is limited to the defining class and subclasses, and `private` is locked strictly to the defining class.

title: Readonly Class Properties
ques: Demonstrate the use of **`readonly`** properties in TypeScript classes alongside parameter properties in the constructor.
explanation: Declaring access modifiers and `readonly` directly in constructor parameter lists is syntactic sugar that automatically initializes immutable class member variables.

title: Abstract Classes and Template Methods
ques: Explain the role of **Abstract Classes** in TypeScript. Create an abstract class `PaymentProcessor` with an abstract method `processPayment(amount: number): boolean` and a concrete child class `StripeProcessor`.
explanation: Abstract classes serve as base classes that cannot be instantiated directly. They define common shared behavior while mandating that child classes implement abstract contract methods.

title: Implementing Interfaces via Implements
ques: Demonstrate how a TypeScript class implements an interface contract using the **`implements`** keyword. Create a `Printable` interface and a `Document` class.
explanation: The `implements` keyword guarantees at compile time that a class adheres to the structural interface contract, implementing all required fields and method signatures.

title: Encapsulating Logic with Getters and Setters
ques: Write a TypeScript class demonstrating **`get`** and **`set`** accessors for a `temperatureCelsius` property that validates data and provides a calculated Fahrenheit conversion.
explanation: Getters and setters intercept property reads and writes, allowing encapsulation, validation, and computed properties while maintaining clean property-access syntax.
